# FlaggedEliminateButLiveNow  (group3.dle)
# FlaggedEliminateButLiveNow ≡ Application ⊓ EliminateRating ⊓ (LiveNow ⊔ LiveNowOpenEnded)
# EliminateRating        ≡ ∃strategicRating.{"Eliminate"}
# LiveNow                ≡ ∃liveStartDate,liveEndDate.enclosesNow
#                           liveStartDate ≤ now() ∧ now() ≤ liveEndDate
# LiveNowOpenEnded       ≡ ∃liveStartDate.onOrBeforeNow ⊓ ¬∃liveEndDate.⊤
#                           liveStartDate ≤ now() ∧ no liveEndDate
#
# LiveNow ⊔ LiveNowOpenEnded simplifies to:
#   liveStartDate ≤ now()  ∧  ¬( liveEndDate exists ∧ liveEndDate < now() )

PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX xsd:          <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

SELECT ?id ?name ?value
WHERE {
  # Required anchor
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .

  # Application
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Application" .

  # EliminateRating: strategicRating = "Eliminate"
  ?strategicRatingField ardoq-common:name "strategic_rating" .
  ?entity ?strategicRatingField "Eliminate" .

  # LiveNow ⊔ LiveNowOpenEnded: liveStartDate must exist and be ≤ now()
  ?liveStartField ardoq-common:name "live_start_date" .
  ?entity ?liveStartField ?liveStart .
  FILTER (?liveStart <= NOW())

  # Bind ?entity positively before the negation
  ?entity ardoq-common:id ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .

  # liveEndField resolved outside so it is bound inside the NOT EXISTS
  ?liveEndField ardoq-common:name "live_end_date" .

  # Exclude entities whose liveEndDate is strictly in the past
  # (no liveEnd, or liveEnd ≥ now(), both pass through)
  FILTER NOT EXISTS {
    ?entity ?liveEndField ?liveEnd .
    FILTER (?liveEnd < NOW())
  }

  BIND("Eliminate" AS ?value)
}

PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>

  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Application" .
  ?entity ardoq-common:id ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .

  ?referenceType rdfs:label "Has Successor" .
  ?referenceType rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Reference .
  ?entity ?referenceType ?entity .

  BIND("Self-loop lifecycle relation" AS ?value)
}

# FlaggedMultipleSuccessors  (group4.dle)
# FlaggedMultipleSuccessors ≡ Application ⊓ (≥2 isSucceededBy.⊤)

PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

SELECT ?id ?name (COUNT(DISTINCT ?successor) AS ?value)
WHERE {
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Application" .
  ?entity ardoq-common:id ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .

  ?referenceType rdfs:label "isSucceededBy" .
  ?referenceType rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Reference .
  ?entity ?referenceType ?successor .
}
GROUP BY ?entity ?id ?name
HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?successor) >= 2)

# FlaggedMultipleReplacements  (group4.dle)
# FlaggedMultipleReplacements ≡ Application ⊓ (≥2 replacedBy.⊤)

PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

SELECT ?id ?name (COUNT(DISTINCT ?replacement) AS ?value)
WHERE {
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Application" .
  ?entity ardoq-common:id ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .

  ?referenceType rdfs:label "replacedBy" .
  ?referenceType rdfs:subClassOf+ ardoq:Reference .
  ?entity ?referenceType ?replacement .
}
GROUP BY ?id ?name
HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?replacement) >= 2)

# FlaggedSucceededAndReplaced  (group4.dle)
# FlaggedSucceededAndReplaced ≡ Application ⊓ ∃isSucceededBy.⊤ ⊓ ∃replacedBy.⊤

PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

SELECT DISTINCT ?id ?name ?value
WHERE {
  # Required anchor
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .

  # Application type constraint
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Application" .

  ?entity ardoq-common:id   ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .

  # ∃isSucceededBy.⊤ — at least one isSucceededBy reference
  ?succType rdfs:label "isSucceededBy" .
  ?succType rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Reference .
  ?entity ?succType ?anySuccessor .

  # ∃replacedBy.⊤ — at least one replacedBy reference
  ?replType rdfs:label "replacedBy" .
  ?replType rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Reference .
  ?entity ?replType ?anyReplacement .

  BIND("FlaggedSucceededAndReplaced" AS ?value)
}

# FlaggedCriticalNoLifecyclePlan  (group4.dle)
# FlaggedCriticalNoLifecyclePlan ≡ Application ⊓ HighCriticality ⊓ ¬∃hasLifecycleRelation.⊤
# HighCriticality ≡ ∃criticality.{"4", "5"}

PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

SELECT ?id ?name ?value
WHERE {
  # Anchor: Application is a Component (Application ⊑ Component ⊑ ardoq:Component)
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Application" .

  # HighCriticality: criticality ∈ {"4", "5"} — declared as string enum
  ?critFieldType ardoq-common:name "criticality" .
  ?entity ?critFieldType ?value .
  FILTER(?value IN ("4", "5"))

  # Positively bind ?entity via id and name before negation
  ?entity ardoq-common:id ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .

  # ¬∃hasLifecycleRelation.⊤ — no outgoing reference of type hasLifecycleRelation
  # or any of its sub-properties (isSucceededBy, replacedBy, hasTimedDependency)
  FILTER NOT EXISTS {
    ?baseLifecycleType rdfs:label "Has Successor" .
    ?baseLifecycleType rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Reference .
    ?lifecycleRefType rdfs:subClassOf* ?baseLifecycleType .
    ?entity ?lifecycleRefType ?target .
  }
}

# FlaggedSuccessorEndedInPast  (group4.dle)
# FlaggedSuccessorEndedInPast ≡ Application ⊓ ∃isSucceededBy.(LiveEndedInPast)
# LiveEndedInPast ≡ ∃liveEndDate.beforeNow
# beforeNow(x) ≝ x < now()
# isSucceededBy ⊑ hasLifecycleRelation; hasLifecycleRelation @db "Has Successor"

PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX xsd:          <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

SELECT ?id ?name ?value
WHERE {
  # Anchor: entity is a Component
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .

  # Entity is an Application
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Application" .

  # Bind id and name (also satisfies the negation-safety requirement)
  ?entity ardoq-common:id ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .

  # Outgoing isSucceededBy reference (stored as "Has Successor")
  ?refType rdfs:label "Has Successor" .
  ?refType rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Reference .
  ?entity ?refType ?successor .

  # Anchor the successor as a Component
  ?successor rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .

  # Successor has a liveEndDate that lies in the past (LiveEndedInPast)
  ?liveEndFieldType ardoq-common:name "live_end_date" .
  ?successor ?liveEndFieldType ?liveEndDate .
  FILTER(?liveEndDate < NOW())

  # Report the successor's name as the flagged value
  ?successor ardoq-common:name ?value .
}

# FlaggedOrphanOrgUnit  (group5.dle)
# FlaggedOrphanOrgUnit ≡ OrganizationalUnit ⊓ ¬∃parent.Organization ⊓ ¬∃partOf.⊤

PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

SELECT ?id ?name ?value WHERE {

  # Anchor
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .

  # Must be an Organizational Unit
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Organizational Unit" .

  # Bind before negations so patterns are evaluated per-entity
  ?entity ardoq-common:id   ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .

  # ¬∃parent.Organization — no direct Organization parent
  FILTER NOT EXISTS {
    ?entity ardoq-common:parent ?parentEntity .
    ?parentEntity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Organization" .
  }

  # ¬∃partOf.⊤ — no outgoing partOf reference to anything
  FILTER NOT EXISTS {
    ?partOfType rdfs:label "Part Of" .
    ?partOfType rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Reference .
    ?entity ?partOfType ?target .
  }

  BIND("FlaggedOrphanOrgUnit" AS ?value)
}

# FlaggedPersonNoOrgUnit  (group5.dle)
PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

# FlaggedPersonNoOrgUnit ≡ Person ⊓ ¬∃belongsTo.⊤

SELECT ?id ?name ?value
WHERE {
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Person" .
  ?entity ardoq-common:id ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .
  ?referenceType rdfs:label "Belongs To" .
  ?referenceType rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Reference .
  FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?entity ?referenceType ?target }
  BIND("FlaggedPersonNoOrgUnit" AS ?value)
}

# FlaggedPersonSelfReports  (group5.dle)
PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

# FlaggedPersonSelfReports ≡ Person ⊓ ∃reportsTo.Self
SELECT ?id ?name ?value
WHERE {
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Person" .
  ?entity ardoq-common:id ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .

  ?referenceType rdfs:label "Reports To" .
  ?referenceType rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Reference .
  ?entity ?referenceType ?entity .

  BIND(true AS ?value)
}

# FlaggedPersonIsolated  (group5.dle)
PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

# FlaggedPersonIsolated ≡ Person ⊓ ¬∃reportsTo.⊤ ⊓ ¬∃(reportsTo⁻).⊤
# Person has no reports, and reports to no one

SELECT ?id ?name ?value
WHERE {
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Person" .
  ?entity ardoq-common:id ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .

  ?referenceType rdfs:label "Reports To" .
  ?referenceType rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Reference .

  FILTER NOT EXISTS {
    ?entity ?referenceType ?target .
  }
  FILTER NOT EXISTS {
    ?source ?referenceType ?entity .
  }

  BIND("FlaggedPersonIsolated" AS ?value)
}

# FlaggedPersonReportingCycle  (group5.dle)
PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

# FlaggedPersonReportingCycle ≡ Person ⊓ ∃subordinateTo.Self
# where: reportsTo ⊑ subordinateTo
#        subordinateTo ∘ subordinateTo ⊑ subordinateTo   (transitivity)
# i.e. a Person who appears in their own reportsTo transitive closure (any reporting cycle)
# SPARQL cannot use a runtime-bound IRI in a property path, so cycles of length 1, 2 and 3
# are enumerated via UNION, covering all practically occurring reporting-chain cycles.

SELECT DISTINCT ?id ?name ?value
WHERE {
  # Required anchor
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .

  # Must be a Person
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Person" .

  ?entity ardoq-common:id   ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .

  # Resolve the "Reports To" reference type
  ?rt rdfs:label "Reports To" .
  ?rt rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Reference .

  # subordinateTo.Self — entity reachable from itself via one or more reportsTo hops
  {
    # Cycle of length 1: person reports directly to themselves
    ?entity ?rt ?entity .
  }
  UNION
  {
    # Cycle of length 2: A → B → A
    ?entity ?rt ?s1 .
    FILTER(?s1 != ?entity)
    ?s1 ?rt ?entity .
  }
  UNION
  {
    # Cycle of length 3: A → B → C → A
    ?entity ?rt ?s1 .
    FILTER(?s1 != ?entity)
    ?s1 ?rt ?s2 .
    FILTER(?s2 != ?entity && ?s2 != ?s1)
    ?s2 ?rt ?entity .
  }
  UNION
  {
    # Cycle of length 4: A → B → C → D → A
    ?entity ?rt ?s1 .
    FILTER(?s1 != ?entity)
    ?s1 ?rt ?s2 .
    FILTER(?s2 != ?entity && ?s2 != ?s1)
    ?s2 ?rt ?s3 .
    FILTER(?s3 != ?entity && ?s3 != ?s1 && ?s3 != ?s2)
    ?s3 ?rt ?entity .
  }

  BIND("Reporting chain is cyclic" AS ?value)
}

# FlaggedManagerHugeSpan  (group5.dle)
# FlaggedManagerHugeSpan ≡ Person ⊓ (≥20 reportsTo⁻.⊤)

PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

SELECT ?id ?name (COUNT(?subordinate) AS ?value)
WHERE {
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Person" .
  ?entity ardoq-common:id ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .

  ?referenceType rdfs:label "Reports To" .
  ?referenceType rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Reference .
  ?subordinate ?referenceType ?entity .
}
GROUP BY ?entity ?id ?name
HAVING (COUNT(?subordinate) >= 20)

# FlaggedMissingName  (group6.dle)
# FlaggedMissingName ≡ Component ⊓ ¬∃name.⊤

PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

SELECT ?id ?name ?value
WHERE {
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .
  ?entity ardoq-common:id ?id .
  FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name }
}

# FlaggedMissingReviewDate  (group6.dle)
# FlaggedMissingReviewDate ≡ (Application ⊔ BusinessCapability) ⊓ ¬∃review_date.⊤

PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>

SELECT ?id ?name ?value
WHERE {
  ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:subClassOf/rdfs:subClassOf ardoq:Component .

  {
    { ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Application" }
    UNION
    { ?entity rdf:type/rdfs:label "Business Capability" }
  }

  ?entity ardoq-common:id ?id .
  ?entity ardoq-common:name ?name .

  ?reviewDateField ardoq-common:name "review_date" .

  FILTER NOT EXISTS {
    ?entity ?reviewDateField ?anyValue .
  }

  BIND("Missing Review Date" AS ?value)
}

8:## Tests needing a running system must use `ardoq.test.ardoq/deftest` (or `ardoq.test.api/deftest`), not plain `clojure.test/deftest`

     2	
     3	One query per Flagged class, one output file per group.
     4	"""
     5	from __future__ import annotations
     6	
     7	import argparse
     8	import re
     9	import sys
    10	from pathlib import Path
    11	
    12	_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
    13	if str(_PROJECT_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    14	    sys.path.insert(0, str(_PROJECT_ROOT))
    15	
    16	from src.pipeline.config import Paths, Models
    17	from src.pipeline.languages import GREMLIN, SPARQL, Language
    18	from src.pipeline.llm_utils import create_client, extract_single_query
    19	
    20	_FLAGGED_RE = re.compile(r"^([a-zA-Z]+) \u2291 Flagged", re.MULTILINE)
    21	
    22	
    23	def _read(path: Path) -> str:
    24	    return path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    25	
    26	
    27	def run(
    28	    source_dir: Path,
    29	    output_dir: Path,
    30	    *,
    31	    lang: Language = GREMLIN,
    32	    force: bool = False,
    33	    test_run: bool = False,
    34	) -> None:
    35	    """Generate one query file per group DL file in source_dir."""
    36	    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    37	
    38	    group_files = sorted(source_dir.glob("group*.dle"))
    39	    if not group_files:
    40	        print(f"[gen-queries] No group*.dle files found in {source_dir.relative_to(_PROJECT_ROOT)}.")
    41	        return
    42	
    43	    core = _read(Paths.foundation_core)
    44	    prompt_template = _read(Paths.prompts / lang.query_prompt)
    45	    client = create_client()
    46	
    47	    for group_file in group_files:
    48	        suffix = re.search(r"(\d+)\.dle$", group_file.name).group(1)
    49	        out_path = output_dir / f"queries{suffix}{lang.extension}"
    50	
    51	        if out_path.exists() and not force:
    52	            print(f"[gen-queries] {out_path.name} already exists, skipping. Use --force to regenerate.")
    53	            continue
    54	
    55	        group_content = _read(group_file)
    56	        flagged_classes = _FLAGGED_RE.findall(group_content)
    57	        if not flagged_classes:
    58	            print(f"[gen-queries] No Flagged classes in {group_file.name}, skipping.")
    59	            continue
    60	
    61	        print(
    62	            f"[gen-queries] {group_file.name}: {len(flagged_classes)} class(es) ...",
    63	            flush=True,
    64	        )
    65	
    66	        with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as out:
    67	            for flagged in flagged_classes:
    68	                print(f"  {flagged} ...", flush=True)
    69	
    70	                user_content = [
    71	                    {"type": "text", "text": f"=== foundation-core.dle ===\n{core}"},
    72	                    {"type": "text", "text": f"=== {group_file.name} ===\n{group_content}"},
    73	                    {"type": "text", "text": prompt_template.format(flagged=flagged)},
    74	                ]
    75	
    76	                with client.messages.stream(
    77	                    model=Models.query_gen,
    78	                    max_tokens=16000,
    79	                    thinking={"type": "enabled", "budget_tokens": 15999},
    80	                    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user_content}],
    81	                ) as stream:
    82	                    response = stream.get_final_message()
    83	
    84	                result_text = next(
    85	                    (b.text for b in response.content if b.type == "text"), None
    86	                )
    87	                if result_text is None:
    88	                    print(f"  WARNING: no text block for {flagged}, skipping.")
    89	                    continue
    90	
    91	                code = extract_single_query(result_text, lang)
    92	                out.write(f"{lang.comment_prefix} {flagged}  ({group_file.name})\n")
    93	                out.write(code)
    94	                out.write("\n\n")
    95	                out.flush()
    96	
    97	                if test_run:
    98	                    print("  --test-run: stopping after first class.")
    99	                    return
   100	
   101	        print(f"  Written: {out_path.relative_to(_PROJECT_ROOT)}")

   105	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
   106	        description="Generate individual queries for Flagged classes."
   107	    )
   108	    parser.add_argument(
   109	        "--source", choices=["inferred", "extended"], default="inferred",
   110	        help="Which group DL directory to read from.",
   111	    )
   112	    parser.add_argument(
   113	        "--lang", choices=["gremlin", "sparql"], default="gremlin",
   114	        help="Which query language to generate.",
   115	    )

   117	    parser.add_argument("--test-run", action="store_true", help="Process only the first class and stop.")

   122	        lang = GREMLIN

   131	    main()
     1	"""Target query languages for the query-generation steps.
     2	
     3	Each language records everything the generation steps need to differ on: the
     4	prompt files, the output file extension, the comment prefix used when writing
     5	headers or commenting out non-query blocks, and how a fenced code block in an
     6	LLM response is recognised as a query.
     7	"""
     8	from __future__ import annotations
     9	
    10	import re
    11	from dataclasses import dataclass
    12	
    13	
    14	@dataclass(frozen=True)
    15	class Language:
    16	    name: str
    17	    query_prompt: str    # prompt for the per-smell step
    18	    report_prompt: str   # prompt for the merged report step
    19	    extension: str
    20	    comment_prefix: str
    21	    fence_tags: tuple[str, ...]   # fence tags that always mean "this is a query"
    22	    query_re: re.Pattern[str]     # detects a query inside a bare ``` fence
    23	
    24	
    25	GREMLIN = Language(
    26	    name="gremlin",
    27	    query_prompt="gen_query.txt",
    28	    report_prompt="gen_report.txt",
    29	    extension=".groovy",
    30	    comment_prefix="//",
    31	    fence_tags=("groovy", "gremlin"),
    32	    query_re=re.compile(r"g\."),
    33	)
    34	
    35	SPARQL = Language(
    36	    name="sparql",
    37	    query_prompt="gen_sparql_query.txt",
    38	    report_prompt="gen_sparql_report.txt",
    39	    extension=".rq",
    40	    comment_prefix="#",
    41	    fence_tags=("sparql",),
    42	    query_re=re.compile(r"(?:PREFIX|SELECT)", re.IGNORECASE),
    43	)

# ardoqbundlesproduction advanced-search harness

Runs the real Ardoq advanced-search reports from the `ardoqbundlesproduction`
tenant against GraphLake, and judges each one against the Postgres numbers the
suite was exported with.

The export (`ardoqbundlesproduction-advanced-search-sparql.txt`) is 275 saved
reports. Each carries the Postgres baseline it was measured at:

```
-- Report: All cloud hosted Applications - CM (baf0a2992029219da12b127a)
-- Postgres: status 200, 85 results, 36.6 ms
PREFIX rdf: ...
SELECT ?entityId WHERE { ... }
```

so every query is scored on two axes: does GraphLake return the same number of
rows, and is it in the same ballpark for time or better.

## Layout

```
ardoqbundles/
  ardoqbundlesproduction-advanced-search-sparql.txt   the export, unmodified
  docker-compose.bundles.yml                          single-node graphlake + sync
  queries/            generated: one .rq per report, plus manifest.json
  reports/            generated: results.<stamp>.json and report.<stamp>.md
  scripts/
    extract-queries.py    export -> queries/ + manifest.json
    start-graphlake.sh    bring the rig up, wait for the sync
    bench_bundles.py      the runner
    run-benchmark.sh      extract + run + report
```

`queries/` and `reports/` are regenerated; the export is the only input.

## Running it

The rig needs the ardoq-docker base stack (postgres, nats) already up, and
locally built `ardoq/graphlake:latest` and `ardoq/graphlake-sync:latest`.

```bash
# 1. build the images from main (from the ardoq-docker runbook)
git -C ../graphlake      worktree add --detach /tmp/gl-build  origin/main
git -C ../graphlake-sync worktree add --detach /tmp/gls-build origin/main
docker build -t ardoq/graphlake:latest      /tmp/gl-build
docker build -t ardoq/graphlake-sync:latest /tmp/gls-build

# 2. fresh single-node graphlake, synced from the running postgres
./ardoqbundles/scripts/start-graphlake.sh fresh

# 3. run the suite
./ardoqbundles/scripts/run-benchmark.sh
```

`run-benchmark.sh` exits non-zero if any runnable query errored or returned a
different number of rows than Postgres, so it is usable as a gate.

## Deliberate choices

**Single node, local backend.** This measures query execution. An orchestrator,
a routing proxy and two replicas add nothing to a read benchmark and add noise
to the timings, so the compose file stands up one node with the local backend
and its own compose project (`glbundles`) on port 7743. It joins the existing
`ardoq_default` network to reach postgres and nats, and touches no container in
the ardoq stack.

**Latest state only — no history replay, no CDC.** `GL_SYNC_FULL_SYNC_HISTORY_REPLAY`
is false and the snapshot mode is off. The reports all query HEAD, so replaying
twelve months of history would cost minutes and change nothing measured here.
The sync still attaches to the shared `DebeziumStream`, under its own consumer
name and with `GL_SYNC_STREAM_RESET_ON_START=false`, so it cannot disturb the
ardoq stack's own sync.

**One warmup, then the median of N runs.** Timings in this repo are warm unless
a note says otherwise; the first query after a write is cold for reasons that
have nothing to do with steady-state query cost.

**"Ballpark" needs a floor as well as a ratio.** Most Postgres baselines here
are single-digit milliseconds, where a 3x ratio is 12ms of nothing. A query is
only reported as *slower* when it is both `--slow-ratio` (default 2x) the
Postgres time **and** at least `--slow-floor-ms` (default 25ms) slower in
absolute terms.

**`--select-distinct`.** The exported SPARQL has no `DISTINCT`, but Ardoq
advanced search dedupes its result set. A report whose `UNION` branches overlap
therefore returns many more rows from GraphLake than Postgres reported — and
pays to materialise them. The default run is faithful to the export; pass
`--select-distinct` for the apples-to-apples comparison. The runner reports
distinct row counts either way, so a query that returns the right *set* with the
wrong multiplicity is classified `duplicate_rows`, not `row_mismatch`.

**12 reports are not run.** They carry no SPARQL: the advanced-search to SPARQL
translation failed upstream (`Unknown operator` on a `between` date rule). That
is a translation gap, not a GraphLake result, so they are listed separately
rather than counted as failures.

## Environment

- `GRAPHLAKE_URL` — default `http://localhost:7743`
- `GRAPHLAKE_STORE` — default `ardoqbundlesproduction`
- `GRAPHLAKE_ADMIN_PASSWORD` — default `ardoq_graphlake_admin_pass`
- `BUNDLES_GRAPHLAKE_HOST_PORT` — default `7743`
- `BUNDLES_RUNS` — timed runs after the warmup; default `5`
- `BUNDLES_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` — per-query timeout; default `120`
- `BUNDLES_TOP` — how many worst queries the report lists; default `10`
PREFIX rdf:          <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs:         <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX ardoq:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/>
PREFIX ardoq-common: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/>
PREFIX xsd:          <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#>
SELECT ?entityId
WHERE {
    ?entity ardoq-common:id ?entityId .
    ?entity (rdf:type / rdfs:subClassOf / rdfs:subClassOf) ardoq:Component .
    ?entity rdf:type ?type244169 .
    ?type244169 rdfs:label "Application" .
    ?entity ardoq-common:id [] .
    FILTER NOT EXISTS {
        [] ?referenceType244170 ?entity .
        ?referenceType244170 (rdfs:subClassOf / rdfs:subClassOf) ardoq:Reference .
        ?referenceType244170 rdfs:label "Is Realized By" .
    }
}

     2	
     3	This document describes the way data is mapped from an ardoq postgresql database into RDF in graphlale. It covers the metamodel, model constructs and instances. Metamodel aligns with the RDF world, e.g. the concepts of Class and Statement, model constructs to mean instances of owl:Class / ComponentType in Ardoq e.g. Person and instances (named individuals), e.g. a specific Person. 
     4	
     5	## Rationale
     6	
     7	In defining this mapping between Ardoq and RDF we have been guided by the following needs and principles.
     8	
     9	+ Support for common query patterns
    10	+ Symmetry and modelling approach for ComponentTypes, ReferenceTypes and FieldTypes
    11	+ Simplicity in the patterns for generating
    12	+ Not requiring inference for basic query operations 
    13	
    14	A full set of query examples can be found further in the document.
    15	
    16	## Identity Rules
    17	
    18	A key part of keeping data in sync, or in general from syncing from another source is that identifiers are unique, they have clear construction rules and non-ambiguous binding back to the original data item in the source system.
    19	
    20	The following patterns show how identifiers for the different kinds of things are constructed.
    21	
    22	```text
    23	Component instance:
    24	  http://data.ardoq.com/instances/components/<component._id>
    25	
    26	References instance:
    27	  http://data.ardoq.com/instances/references/<reference._id>
    28	
    29	Concrete component type class:
    30	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/component-types/<component_type._id>
    31	
    32	Common component name class:
    33	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/component-types/<uuidv5("http://data.ardoq.com/model/component-types/name:" + component_type.name)>
    34	
    35	Concrete reference type property:
    36	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/reference-types/<reference_type._id>
    37	
    38	Common reference name property:
    39	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/reference-types/<uuidv5("http://data.ardoq.com/model/reference-types/name:" + reference_type.name)>
    40	
    41	Global field property:
    42	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/field-types/<global_field._id>
    43	
    44	Model field (a field's placement in one model):
    45	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/model-fields/<field_id_by_model._id>
    46	
    47	Built-in common property:
    48	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/<field-name>
    49	
    50	SHACL shape:
    51	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/shapes/<deterministic-shape-guid>
    52	
    53	Workspace instance:
    54	  http://data.ardoq.com/instances/workspaces/<workspace._id>
    55	
    56	Tag instance:
    57	  http://data.ardoq.com/instances/tags/<tag._id>
    58	
    59	User instance:
    60	  http://data.ardoq.com/instances/users/<user_account._id>
    61	```
    62	
    63	The common component and reference resources are name-level resources. They are created for consistency even when there is only one concrete type with that name.
    64	
    65	Example exact UUIDv5 values used below:
    66	
    67	```text
    68	Common component class for "Application":
    69	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/component-types/a0a27382-298e-574f-a571-dea6ea4cd2ca
    70	
    71	Common component class for "Server":
    72	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/component-types/260b81a3-9c29-57e1-87a4-90a77eb453c8
    73	
    74	Common reference property for "deployed on":
    75	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/reference-types/fd3203a9-9f55-5d50-a1fc-ffc4d1162da3
    76	```
    77	
    78	
    79	## Vocabulary
    80	
    81	The syncer emits RDF/RDFS/OWL/SHACL resources. Below is a list of these for reference:
    82	
    83	```text
    84	rdf:type             http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type
    85	rdfs:label           http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#label
    86	rdfs:comment         http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#comment
    87	rdfs:subClassOf      http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#subClassOf
    88	rdfs:subPropertyOf   http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#subPropertyOf
    89	rdfs:domain          http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#domain
    90	rdfs:range           http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#range
    91	owl:Class            http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#Class
    92	owl:DatatypeProperty http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#DatatypeProperty
    93	owl:ObjectProperty   http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#ObjectProperty
    94	sh:NodeShape         http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#NodeShape
    95	sh:PropertyShape     http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#PropertyShape
    96	sh:targetClass       http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#targetClass
    97	sh:property          http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#property
    98	sh:path              http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#path
    99	sh:datatype          http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#datatype
   100	sh:class             http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#class
   101	xsd:string           http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string
   102	xsd:decimal          http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#decimal
   103	xsd:integer          http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer
   104	xsd:boolean          http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#boolean
   105	xsd:dateTime         http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#dateTime
   106	xsd:date             http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#date
   107	xsd:anyURI           http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#anyURI
   108	```
   109	
   110	One datatype is GraphLake's rather than the W3C's, for a pair of dates or
   111	dateTimes carried as one ISO 8601 interval. Its two accessors sit under a
   112	separate namespace:
   113	
   114	```text
   115	glType:iso8601-date-interval  http://graphlake.net/types/iso8601-date-interval
   116	gl:intervalStart              http://graphlake.net/functions/intervalStart
   117	gl:intervalEnd                http://graphlake.net/functions/intervalEnd
   118	```
   119	
   120	### Prefixes
   121	
   122	The Turtle examples in the rest of this document are written against the following prefixes. The prefix block itself is omitted from each example to keep them short:
   123	
   124	```turtle
   125	@prefix rdf:            <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .
   126	@prefix rdfs:           <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
   127	@prefix owl:            <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .
   128	@prefix sh:             <http://www.w3.org/ns/shacl#> .
   129	@prefix xsd:            <http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#> .
   130	@prefix aqModel:        <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/> .
   131	@prefix aqCommon:       <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/> .
   132	@prefix aqCompType:     <http://data.ardoq.com/model/component-types/> .
   133	@prefix aqRefType:      <http://data.ardoq.com/model/reference-types/> .
   134	@prefix aqFieldType:    <http://data.ardoq.com/model/field-types/> .
   135	@prefix aqModelField:   <http://data.ardoq.com/model/model-fields/> .
   136	@prefix aqShape:        <http://data.ardoq.com/model/shapes/> .
   137	@prefix aqComponent:    <http://data.ardoq.com/instances/components/> .
   138	@prefix aqRefStatement: <http://data.ardoq.com/instances/references/> .
   139	@prefix aqTag:          <http://data.ardoq.com/model/tags/> .
   140	@prefix aqWorkspace:    <http://data.ardoq.com/instances/workspaces/> .
   141	@prefix aqUser:         <http://data.ardoq.com/instances/users/> .
   142	@prefix glType:         <http://graphlake.net/types/> .
   143	@prefix gl:             <http://graphlake.net/functions/> .
   144	```
   145	
   146	When we are generating SHACL shapes the IRIs used are deterministic:
   147	
   148	```text
   149	Node shape:
   150	  uuidv5(URL, "http://data.ardoq.com/model/shapes/node:" + targetClassIRI)
   151	
   152	Data property shape:
   153	  uuidv5(URL, "http://data.ardoq.com/model/shapes/data-property:" + propertyIRI)
   154	
   155	Object property shape:
   156	  uuidv5(URL, "http://data.ardoq.com/model/shapes/object-property:" + sourceClassIRI + "\x00" + propertyIRI + "\x00" + targetClassIRI)
   157	```
   158	
   159	
   160	## Meta Model
   161	
   162	The Meta Model represents the core constructs that can be used to construct a model (a set of classes and property classes). In Ardoq terms ComponentType, ReferenceType and in RDFS terms these align to Class and Property.
   163	
   164	```text
   165	@prefix rdf:             <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .
   166	@prefix rdfs:            <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
   167	@prefix owl:             <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .
   168	@prefix aq:              <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/> .
   169	
   170	# Used to indicate which classes are sourced from Ardoq Component Types
   171	aq:ComponentType a owl:Class .
   172	
   173	# Used to indicate which property classes are sourced from Ardoq Reference Types
   174	aq:ReferenceType a owl:Class .
   175	
   176	# The type of all Ardoq components. The common super class of all ardoq defined Component Types. 
   177	aq:Component a owl:Class .
   178	
   179	# The type of all Ardoq references and hence all RDF reifiers. The common super class of all ardoq defined Reference Types. 
   180	aq:Reference a owl:Class, owl:ObjectProperty .
   181	
   182	# Used to indicate all property classes that are fields defined in ardoq, both buit in and user defined.
   183	aq:FieldType a owl:Class .
   184	
   185	aq:CustomFieldType a owl:Class ;
   186	  rdfs:subClassOf aq:FieldType .
   187	
   188	aq:BuiltInFieldType a owl:Class ;
   189	  rdfs:subClassOf aq:FieldType .
   190	
   191	# The type of all Ardoq fields and hence any RDF reifiers of those statements. The common super class of all ardoq defined Field Types.
   192	aq:Field a owl:Class, owl:DatatypeProperty .
   193	
   194	# A field as it appears in one model: which model it belongs to, and where it sits
   195	# in that model's field list. See the Model Fields section for why this is a
   196	# resource rather than two more predicates on the field type.
   197	aq:ModelField a owl:Class .
   198	```
   199	
   200	## Example
   201	
   202	```text
   203	Verified to be EL/QL/RL/DL valid:
   204	
   205	@prefix rdf:             <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .
   206	@prefix rdfs:            <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
   207	@prefix owl:             <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .
   208	@prefix aq:              <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/> .
   209	@prefix aqCommon:        <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/> .
   210	@prefix aqComponent:     <http://data.ardoq.com/instances/components/> .
   211	@prefix aqReference:     <http://data.ardoq.com/instances/references/> .
   212	@prefix aqComponentType: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/component-types/> .
   213	@prefix aqReferenceType: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/reference-types/> .

   237	### Examples
   238	
   239	# This is an example of a Ardoq defined component type.
   240	# For _reasons_ it's split across a global and a workspace local type.
   241	# It is itself a component type of course, but it's also a subclass of
   242	# aq:Component, such that all instances of this type are also instances of aq:Component.
   243	aqComponentType:global001 a aq:ComponentType, owl:Class ;
   244	  rdfs:subClassOf aq:Component .
   245	
   246	# The local type is a subclass of the global type, so that any instance
   247	# are also instances of the global type.
   248	aqComponentType:local001 a aq:ComponentType, owl:Class ;
   249	  rdfs:subClassOf aqComponentType:global001 .

   251	# Example of a user-defined component.

   253	  aqCommon:id "001" .

   255	## References
   256	
   257	# Example of a user-defined reference type. Same as for component types, it's
   258	# split into local and global. It's both a class and a property, because it
   259	# will be used as predicate for the reified triple, and type for the reifier.
   260	# It's also both a subclass and subproperty of aq:Reference, so that
   261	# instances and triples get the relevant supertype and superproperty inferred.
   262	aqReferenceType:global001 a aq:ReferenceType, owl:ObjectProperty, owl:Class ;
   263	  rdfs:subClassOf aq:Reference ;
   264	  rdfs:subPropertyOf aq:Reference .
   265	
   266	aqReferenceType:local001 a aq:ReferenceType, owl:ObjectProperty, owl:Class ;
   267	  rdfs:subClassOf aqReferenceType:global001 ;
   268	  rdfs:subPropertyOf aqReferenceType:global001 .
   269	
   270	# Here's an example of a reference. The reference entity is the reifier, but
   271	# the triple it reifies is necessary to be able to traverse the graph.
   272	aqComponent:001 aqReferenceType:local001 aqComponent:001 ~ aqReference:001 {|
   273	  a aqReferenceType:local001 ;
   274	  aqCommon:id "001"
   275	|} .
   276	
   277	# With this, we should have inferred triples like:
   278	#   aqComponent:001 aq:Reference aqComponent:001
   279	#   aqReference:001 a aq:Reference
   280	#   aqComponent:001 a aq:Component
   281	# These can all be inferred by RDFS reasoning, but we have taken care to ensure
   282	# the model is also OWL 2 EL/QL/RL/DL compliant, so more advanced reasoning can
   283	# be applied if needed
   284	```

   286	## Users
   287	
   288	A user is the author of a row: `common/createdBy` and `common/lastModifiedBy` are
   289	`owl:ObjectProperty` edges to a `common/User`, not string literals.
   290	
   291	The edit pair is named asymmetrically: the time is `common/lastUpdated` and the
   292	user is `common/lastModifiedBy`, which is how the rest of the platform names
   293	them and what the source columns are called. Advanced search filters the user
   294	under "last modified by", so a predicate named after the timestamp would match
   295	nothing and the endpoint would answer zero rows with an HTTP 200.
   296	
   297	```text
   298	
   299	# User class:
   300	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/User
   301	
   302	# User instance:
   303	  http://data.ardoq.com/instances/users/<user_account._id>
   304	
   305	# Properties:
   306	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/id      user_account._id
   307	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/name    user_account.name
   308	
   309	# Edges to it, from a component, a reference reifier or a workspace:
   310	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/createdBy
   311	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/lastModifiedBy
   312	
   313	```
   314	
   315	**The users come from `public.user_account` in the Ardoq settings database**, the
   316	one `GL_SYNC_ARDOQ_DB_URI` points at. An Ardoq org schema has no `user` table: its
   317	audit columns carry a bare `user_account._id` and nothing else, so the display name
   318	a person searches by is reachable only from there. The name is the reason to write
   319	the resource at all — a User carrying only its id told a query nothing the
   320	`createdBy` edge had not already said.
   321	
   322	Which rows of that table is the whole of the design, because the settings database
   323	is shared by every organisation on an installation. Two things scope it, and both
   324	are needed:
   325	
   326	- **The organisation's people** — `organization.members` and
   327	  `organization.contributors`, jsonb objects keyed by `user_account._id`. This is
   328	  what puts a person in the graph before they have touched anything.
   329	- **The organisation's authors** — every id in an audit column of its schema,
   330	  member or not. Without this an author who has left would resolve to nothing and
   331	  their `createdBy` edges would point at an IRI carrying no triples, which the SHACL
   332	  shape declaring `createdBy`'s range to be `User` makes a violation rather than
   333	  merely a gap. Advanced search resolves an author the same way: a join to the users
   334	  table with no membership filter.
   335	
   336	Neither half reaches outside the organisation: one is its own row, the other its own
   337	data.
   338	
   339	**An author id with no row still gets its resource**, carrying the id and no name.
   340	Only a hard-deleted account gets there — `user_account` has a delete trigger, and
   341	deleting the row does not clear the id out of the audit columns of everything that
   342	person touched, so those ids outlive the row for ever. The resource is written
   343	anyway because the `createdBy` edge pointing at it already exists, and the SHACL
   344	shape for `createdBy` declares its range to be `User`: an edge into an IRI carrying
   345	no triples is a violation on every row that person authored, which is strictly worse
   346	than a resource with no name. The last known name is still in
   347	`user_account__history`, but the syncer's Postgres role has no grant on that
   348	table.
   349	
   350	One consequence worth knowing: a deleted account and a live user whose `name` is
   351	null produce exactly the same two triples, so the graph cannot tell them apart.
   352	
   353	`user_account.name` is nullable, so a user without one gets no `common/name` triple
   354	rather than an empty literal. Nothing else on the row is read — it also holds an
   355	email address, a password hash and SAML/SCIM identifiers, none of which belong in a
   356	graph store.
   357	
   358	A user is written once per target rather than once per row, for the same reason the
   359	model-level triples are: both bulk paths send `X-GraphLake-Skip-Duplicate-Check`, so
   360	a resource re-asserted per component would be *stored* per component. There is no
   361	update or delete mapping for one — a full sync rewrites the directory, and the
   362	streaming path re-asserts an author when it sees one of their rows.
   363	
   364	The id is percent-escaped when minting the IRI. Unlike a component or reference id
   365	it is minted from an audit column as often as from the user row, and nothing
   366	validates an audit column, so one stray space would otherwise produce a malformed
   367	IRI and fail the whole update.
   368	
   369	Example source rows:
   370	
   371	```text
   372	user_account._id          u-ada
   373	user_account.name         Ada Lovelace
   374	
   375	component._id             app-001
   376	component.createdBy       u-ada
   377	component.lastModifiedBy  u-grace
   378	```
   379	
   380	Example triples:
   381	
   382	```turtle
   383	aqUser:u-ada a aqCommon:User ;
   384	  aqCommon:id   "u-ada" ;
   385	  aqCommon:name "Ada Lovelace" .
   386	
   387	aqComponent:app-001
   388	  aqCommon:createdBy      aqUser:u-ada ;
   389	  aqCommon:lastModifiedBy aqUser:u-grace .
   390	```
   391	
   392	Both edges are cleared by `del_component_metadata` and `del_reference_metadata`,
   393	alongside `rdf:type`, `common/parent` and `common/workspace`, because
   394	`del_all_about` removes only literal-object triples: a row that changed hands would
   395	otherwise name both authors.
   396	
   397	Being object-valued has one model-level consequence. `common/createdBy` and
   398	`common/lastModifiedBy` are no longer `aq:BuiltInFieldType` and no longer sit under
   399	`aq:Field`. `aq:Field` is an `owl:DatatypeProperty`, and OWL 2 DL requires object
   400	and data properties to be disjoint, so an object-valued built-in cannot be a
   401	sub-property of it — the same reason `common/parent` and `common/workspace` are not.
   402	Their SHACL shapes are `sh:class common/User` rather than `sh:datatype xsd:string`.
   403	
   404	`global_field.type = 'User'` values are still `xsd:string`. They are user ids too
   405	and should become edges to these same resources; that is not mapped yet.
   406	
   407	### Emitting a user exactly once
   408	
   409	The resources are emitted **once per target**, never per row. Both bulk paths send
   410	`X-GraphLake-Skip-Duplicate-Check`, which turns off GraphLake's duplicate check, so
   411	a type triple asserted once per component would be *stored* once per component: on
   412	this repo's dev org that is 33,716 copies of one triple for a single user. Each
   413	path uses its own mechanism:
   414	
   415	```text
   416	full sync         one directory read, before components, per target (main and each
   417	                  branch, since each commits by MOVEing its own graph over the
   418	                  target's live graph). The author half of its scope is a `select
   419	                  distinct` over the audit columns of the live tables
   420	history backfill  the same, with the author pass reading the history mirrors as
   421	                  well. Recorded once before the first month as one `user:<id>`
   422	                  entity in the carried state, and written nowhere else: a month's
   423	                  snapshot is materialised from that state, and the backfill does
   424	                  not touch the head
   425	CDC streaming     per row, resolving each author against the settings database
   426	                  through a cache that holds misses as well as hits. This is the
   427	                  only path that can add a user between full syncs: the CDC stream
   428	                  carries the org schema, and the directory is elsewhere. It does
   429	                  not skip the duplicate check, so the store collapses the repeats
   430	```
   431	
   432	The two author passes differ deliberately. A full sync writes live state, so a
   433	live-only pass is right. Replay materialises entities that have since been deleted —
   434	a component removed last year is written into every month before its deletion — and
   435	its author may appear in no live row, so a live-only pass there would leave that
   436	component's `createdBy` edge pointing at an untyped IRI.
   437	
   438	A replayed snapshot carries today's names, not the names the organisation's people
   439	had in that month. `user_account` is a live table with no per-month view, and the
   440	membership maps have none either.
   441	
   442	Duplicate stored triples are invisible to SPARQL — GraphLake filters duplicates on
   443	read — so this is a write-amplification and storage concern, not a correctness one,
   444	and no query can detect a regression. The guard is
   445	`TestBulkPathNeverTypesAUserPerRow`, which asserts on the op stream instead.
   446	
   447	### Emitting a shared model resource exactly once
   448	
   449	The same problem applies to every model-level resource more than one row reaches,
   450	and for the same reason: the builders assert them from each row so a single CDC
   451	change event stands alone. On the bulk paths those repeats are stored.
   452	
   453	```text
   454	common reference-type triples   asserted by every reference_type row of that name
   455	name-level component class      asserted by every component_type row of that name
   456	concrete type node shape        asserted by the type, and again by every field
   457	                                attached to it and every org_triple that targets it
   458	```
   459	
   460	**All three paths** filter their ops through `assertedModelTriples`, which drops the
   461	second and later assertion of any triple whose subject can be reached from more than
   462	one row. Two kinds can: anything under `http://data.ardoq.com/model/`, and a User,
   463	which is the one individual with no row of its own.
   464	
   465	Every other instance subject is deliberately excluded. A component, reference, tag
   466	or workspace subject is asserted by exactly one row, so there is nothing to collapse
   467	— and remembering them would grow the set with row count instead of with model size,
   468	which is the whole point. What is held is bounded by the model plus the number of
   469	distinct authors.
   470	
   471	The three pattern deletes (`del_all_about`, `del_component_metadata`,
   472	`del_reference_metadata`) are always scoped to an instance subject, so they can
   473	never remove a remembered triple behind the filter's back.
   474	
   475	Lifetimes differ by path, because what invalidates the record differs:
   476	
   477	```text
   478	full sync      one record per target, held for the run and discarded with it, so an
   479	               aborted sync cannot leave a claim about a graph that was thrown away
   480	history backfill  one record per staged month, because a month is staged whole:
   481	               the walk of the carried state repeats the shared model triples once
   482	               per entity that references them, and the record collapses those
   483	streaming      per target, held for the process. Committed only after the write
   484	               lands, so a naked message's redelivery re-asserts what never arrived
   485	```
   486	
   487	The streaming path is the one where this recurs rather than happening once: every
   488	change event carries the shared triples, so before filtering a 25-event run sent 49
   489	duplicates in 253 add-ops. The standing measurements are
   490	`TestStreamingSendsNoDuplicateTriples` and
   491	`TestBulkModelPassesSendNoDuplicateTriples`, which fail with a count. The full sync
   492	also logs `model_triples` and `duplicate_model_ops_collapsed` per schema.
   493	
   494	One duplicate is left, and is intrinsic. N references between the same pair with the
   495	same type are N reifiers over one plain edge, and each asserts that edge. It is
   496	genuinely shared: GraphLake removes it when the last reifier goes, and does so by an
   497	existence check on `rdf:reifies` rather than by a reference count
   498	(`core.collectReifierOrphans`), so nothing needs to know how many asserted it.
   499	
   500	What that costs differs by path, because the store's duplicate check is on in one and
   501	off in the others:
   502	
   503	```text
   504	streaming         the edge is sent N times and stored once (check on)
   505	full sync         sent N times and stored N times (check off)
   506	history backfill  staged once per month: the carried state holds one copy of the
   507	                  edge, and the walk that materialises the month collapses the
   508	                  repeats before staging
   509	```
   510	
   511	Collapsing it would mean remembering instance triples, whose count scales with rows
   512	rather than with parallel edges — see `isSharedSubject`. It is pinned instead, with
   513	its exact count, by `TestParallelReferencesShareOnePlainEdge`: if anything else began
   514	repeating, that count would rise and the test fails.
   515	
   516	Every other path is audited to zero, per path rather than in aggregate:
   517	`TestStreamingSendsNoDuplicateTriples`,
   518	`TestBulkModelPassesSendNoDuplicateTriples`,
   519	`TestSnapshotHistoryReplayStagesNoDuplicateTriples` and
   520	`TestIncrementalHistoryReplaySendsNoDuplicateTriples`.
   521	
   522	
   523	Two limits worth knowing. Every target gets the whole org's user set, so a branch
   524	holds a few User resources it does not reference; the alternative is a per-branch
   525	pass over a set that barely varies by branch. And a user who leaves the
   526	organisation, or is removed from `user_account` entirely, keeps their resource until
   527	the next full sync — nothing enumerates users to retract them, exactly as a
   528	workspace delete leaves the edges pointing at it.

   530	## Workspaces
   531	
   532	Workspaces are modelled explicitly and also as a string property on components and references. This is to facilitate explicit use of workspace ids and be backwards compatible with gremlin graph queries which treat workspace as a string property on nodes.
   533	
   534	```text
   535	
   536	# Workspace class:
   537	  http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/Workspace
   538	
   539	# Workspace instance:
   540	  http://data.ardoq.com/instances/workspaces/<workspace._id>
   541	
   542	# Edge to the workspace, from a component or a reference reifier:
   543	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/workspace
   544	
   545	# The same value as a literal, for gremlin parity:
   546	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/rootWorkspace
   547	
   548	```
   549	
   550	`Workspace` sits at the meta level next to `Tag`, for the same reason: its members
   551	are individuals a customer created, not model constructs. No concrete type row
   552	mints it and no shape targets it.
   553	
   554	The literal and the edge are two IRIs, not one. OWL 2 DL keeps object and data
   555	properties disjoint — "no IRI is declared to be both object and data property" —
   556	so `common/rootWorkspace` stays the `owl:DatatypeProperty` gremlin queries read,
   557	and `common/workspace` is the `owl:ObjectProperty` that points at the resource.
   558	Both are built from the one `rootWorkspace` column, so they cannot name different
   559	workspaces.
   560	
   561	A workspace individual carries the same built-ins a component does, rather than a
   562	second spelling of name and description:
   563	
   564	```text
   565	workspace._id            aqCommon:id
   566	workspace.name           aqCommon:name
   567	workspace.description    aqCommon:description
   568	w

150	   150	  uuidv5(URL, "http://data.ardoq.com/model/shapes/node:" + targetClassIRI)
151	   151	
152	   152	Data property shape:
153	   153	  uuidv5(URL, "http://data.ardoq.com/model/shapes/data-property:" + propertyIRI)
154	   154	
155	   155	Object property shape:
156	   156	  uuidv5(URL, "http://data.ardoq.com/model/shapes/object-property:" + sourceClassIRI + "\x00" + propertyIRI + "\x00" + targetClassIRI)
157	   157	```
158	   158	
159	   159	
160	   160	## Meta Model
161	   161	
162	   162	The Meta Model represents the core constructs that can be used to construct a model (a set of classes and property classes). In Ardoq terms ComponentType, ReferenceType and in RDFS terms these align to Class and Property.
163	   163	
164	   164	```text
165	   165	@prefix rdf:             <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .
166	   166	@prefix rdfs:            <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
167	   167	@prefix owl:             <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .
168	   168	@prefix aq:              <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/> .
169	   169	
170	   170	# Used to indicate which classes are sourced from Ardoq Component Types
171	   171	aq:ComponentType a owl:Class .
172	   172	
173	   173	# Used to indicate which property classes are sourced from Ardoq Reference Types
174	   174	aq:ReferenceType a owl:Class .
175	   175	
176	   176	# The type of all Ardoq components. The common super class of all ardoq defined Component Types. 
177	   177	aq:Component a owl:Class .
178	   178	
179	   179	# The type of all Ardoq references and hence all RDF reifiers. The common super class of all ardoq defined Reference Types. 
180	   180	aq:Reference a owl:Class, owl:ObjectProperty .
181	   181	
182	   182	# Used to indicate all property classes that are fields defined in ardoq, both buit in and user defined.
183	   183	aq:FieldType a owl:Class .
184	   184	
185	   185	aq:CustomFieldType a owl:Class ;
186	   186	  rdfs:subClassOf aq:FieldType .
187	   187	
188	   188	aq:BuiltInFieldType a owl:Class ;
189	   189	  rdfs:subClassOf aq:FieldType .
190	   190	
191	   191	# The type of all Ardoq fields and hence any RDF reifiers of those statements. The common super class of all ardoq defined Field Types.
192	   192	aq:Field a owl:Class, owl:DatatypeProperty .
193	   193	
194	   194	# A field as it appears in one model: which model it belongs to, and where it sits
195	   195	# in that model's field list. See the Model Fields section for why this is a
196	   196	# resource rather than two more predicates on the field type.
197	   197	aq:ModelField a owl:Class .
198	   198	```
199	   199	
200	   200	## Example
201	   201	
202	   202	```text
203	   203	Verified to be EL/QL/RL/DL valid:
204	   204	
205	   205	@prefix rdf:             <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#> .
206	   206	@prefix rdfs:            <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#> .
207	   207	@prefix owl:             <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#> .
208	   208	@prefix aq:              <http://data.ardoq.com/meta-model/> .
209	   209	@prefix aqCommon:        <http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/> .
210	   210	@prefix aqComponent:     <http://data.ardoq.com/instances/components/> .
211	   211	@prefix aqReference:     <http://data.ardoq.com/instances/references/> .
212	   212	@prefix aqComponentType: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/component-types/> .
213	   213	@prefix aqReferenceType: <http://data.ardoq.com/model/reference-types/> .
214	   214	
215	   215	### Meta Model
216	   216	aq:ComponentType a owl:Class .
217	   217	aq:ReferenceType a owl:Class .
218	   218	aq:Component a owl:Class .
219	   219	aq:Reference a owl:Class, owl:ObjectProperty .
220	   220	aq:FieldType a owl:Class .
221	   221	aq:CustomFieldType a owl:Class ;
222	   222	  rdfs:subClassOf aq:FieldType .
223	   223	aq:BuiltInFieldType a owl:Class ;
224	   224	  rdfs:subClassOf aq:FieldType .
225	   225	aq:Field a owl:Class, owl:DatatypeProperty .
226	   226	aq:ModelField a owl:Class .
227	   227	
228	   228	### Built In Model Constructs
229	   229	
230	   230	aqCommon:id a aq:BuiltInFieldType, owl:Class, owl:DatatypeProperty ;
231	   231	  rdfs:subClassOf aq:Field ;
232	   232	  rdfs:subPropertyOf aq:Field .
233	   233	
234	   234	# aqCommon:name, created, description, createdBy, all follow the same pattern.
235	   235	# These are all pulled from the component and reference table in Ardoq
236	   236	
237	   237	### Examples
238	   238	
239	   239	# This is an example of a Ardoq defined component type.
240	   240	# For _reasons_ it's split across a global and a workspace local type.
241	   241	# It is itself a component type of course, but it's also a subclass of
242	   242	# aq:Component, such that all instances of this type are also instances of aq:Component.
243	   243	aqComponentType:global001 a aq:ComponentType, owl:Class ;
244	   244	  rdfs:subClassOf aq:Component .
245	   245	
246	   246	# The local type is a subclass of the global type, so that any instance
247	   247	# are also instances of the global type.
248	   248	aqComponentType:local001 a aq:ComponentType, owl:Class ;
249	   249	  rdfs:subClassOf aqComponentType:global001 .
250	   250	
251	   251	# Example of a user-defined component.
252	   252	aqComponent:001 a aqComponentType:local001 ;
253	   253	  aqCommon:id "001" .
254	   254	
255	   255	## References
256	   256	
257	   257	# Example of a user-defined reference type. Same as for component types, it's
258	   258	# split into local and global. It's both a class and a property, because it
259	   259	# will be used as predicate for the reified triple, and type for the reifier.
260	   260	# It's also both a subclass and subproperty of aq:Reference, so that
261	   261	# instances and triples get the relevant supertype and superproperty inferred.
262	   262	aqReferenceType:global001 a aq:ReferenceType, owl:ObjectProperty, owl:Class ;
263	   263	  rdfs:subClassOf aq:Reference ;
264	   264	  rdfs:subPropertyOf aq:Reference .
265	   265	
266	   266	aqReferenceType:local001 a aq:ReferenceType, owl:ObjectProperty, owl:Class ;
267	   267	  rdfs:subClassOf aqReferenceType:global001 ;
268	   268	  rdfs:subPropertyOf aqReferenceType:global001 .
269	   269	
270	   270	# Here's an example of a reference. The reference entity is the reifier, but
271	   271	# the triple it reifies is necessary to be able to traverse the graph.
272	   272	aqComponent:001 aqReferenceType:local001 aqComponent:001 ~ aqReference:001 {|
273	   273	  a aqReferenceType:local001 ;
274	   274	  aqCommon:id "001"
275	   275	|} .
276	   276	
277	   277	# With this, we should have inferred triples like:
278	   278	#   aqComponent:001 aq:Reference aqComponent:001
279	   279	#   aqReference:001 a aq:Reference
280	   280	#   aqComponent:001 a aq:Component
281	   281	# These can all be inferred by RDFS reasoning, but we have taken care to ensure
282	   282	# the model is also OWL 2 EL/QL/RL/DL compliant, so more advanced reasoning can
283	   283	# be applied if needed
284	   284	```
285	   285	
286	   286	## Users
287	   287	
288	   288	A user is the author of a row: `common/createdBy` and `common/lastModifiedBy` are
289	   289	`owl:ObjectProperty` edges to a `common/User`, not string literals.
290	   290	
291	   291	The edit pair is named asymmetrically: the time is `common/lastUpdated` and the
292	   292	user is `common/lastModifiedBy`, which is how the rest of the platform names
293	   293	them and what the source columns are called. Advanced search filters the user
294	   294	under "last modified by", so a predicate named after the timestamp would match
295	   295	nothing and the endpoint would answer zero rows with an HTTP 200.
296	   296	
297	   297	```text
298	   298	
299	   299	# User class:
300	   300	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/User
301	   301	
302	   302	# User instance:
303	   303	  http://data.ardoq.com/instances/users/<user_account._id>
304	   304	
305	   305	# Properties:
306	   306	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/id      user_account._id
307	   307	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/name    user_account.name
308	   308	
309	   309	# Edges to it, from a component, a reference reifier or a workspace:
310	   310	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/createdBy
311	   311	  http://data.ardoq.com/model/common/lastModifiedBy
312	   312	
313	   313	```
314	   314	
315	   315	**The users come from `public.user_account` in the Ardoq settings database**, the
316	   316	one `GL_SYNC_ARDOQ_DB_URI` points at. An Ardoq org schema has no `user` table: its
317	   317	audit columns carry a bare `user_account._id` and nothing else, so the display name
318	   318	a person searches by is reachable only from there. The name is the reason to write
319	   319	the resource at all — a User carrying only its id told a query nothing the
320	   320	`createdBy` edge had not already said.
321	   321	
322	   322	Which rows of that table is the whole of the design, because the settings database
323	   323	is shared by every organisation on an installation. Two things scope it, and both
324	   324	are needed:
325	   325	
326	   326	- **The organisation's people** — `organization.members` and
327	   327	  `organization.contributors`, jsonb objects keyed by `user_account._id`. This is
328	   328	  what puts a person in the graph before they have touched anything.
329	   329	- **The organisation's authors** — every id in an audit column of its schema,
330	   330	  member or not. Without this an author who has left would resolve to nothing and
331	   331	  their `createdBy` edges would point at an IRI carrying no triples, which the SHACL
332	   332	  shape declaring `createdBy`'s range to be `User` makes a violation rather than
333	   333	  merely a gap. Advanced search resolves an author the same way: a join to the users
334	   334	  table with no membership filter.
335	   335	
336	   336	Neither half reaches outside the organisation: one is its own row, the other its own
337	   337	data.
338	   338	
339	   339	**An author id with no row still gets its resource**, carrying the id and no name.
340	   340	Only a hard-deleted account gets there — `user_account` has a delete trigger, and
341	   341	deleting the row does not clear the id out of the audit columns of everything that
342	   342	person touched, so those ids outlive the row for ever. The resource is written
343	   343	anyway because the `createdBy` edge pointing at it already exists, and the SHACL
344	   344	shape for `createdBy` declares its range to be `User`: an edge into an IRI carrying
345	   345	no triples is a violation on every row that person authored, which is strictly worse
346	   346	than a resource with no name. The last known name is still in
347	   347	`user_account__history`, but the syncer's Postgres role has no grant on that
348	   348	table.
349	   349	
350	   350	One consequence worth knowing: a deleted account and a live user whose `name` is
351	   351	null produce exactly the same two triples, so the graph cannot tell them apart.
352	   352	
353	   353	`user_account.name` is nullable, so a user without one gets no `common/name` triple
354	   354	rather than an empty literal. Nothing else on the row is read — it also holds an
355	   355	email address, a password hash and SAML/SCIM identifiers, none of which belong in a
356	   356	graph store.
357	   357	
358	   358	A user is written once per target rather than once per row, for the same reason the
359	   359	model-level triples are: both bulk paths send `X-GraphLake-Skip-Duplicate-Check`, so
360	   360	a resource re-asserted per component would be *stored* per component. There is no
361	   361	update or delete mapping for one — a full sync rewrites the directory, and the
362	   362	streaming path re-asserts an author when it sees one of their rows.
363	   363	
364	   364	The id is percent-escaped when minting the IRI. Unlike a component or reference id
365	   365	it is minted from an audit column as often as from the user row, and nothing
366	   366	validates an audit column, so one stray space would otherwise produce a malformed
367	   367	IRI and fail the whole update.
368	   368	
369	   369	Example source rows:
370	   370	
371	   371	```text
372	   372	user_account._id          u-ada
373	   373	user_account.name         Ada Lovelace
374	   374	
375	   375	component._id             app-001
376	   376	component.createdBy       u-ada
377	   377	component.lastModifiedBy  u-grace
378	   378	```
379	   379	
380	   380	Example triples:
381	   381	
382	   382	```turtle
383	   383	aqUser:u-ada a aqCommon:User ;
384	   384	  aqCommon:id   "u-ada" ;
385	   385	  aqCommon:name "Ada Lovelace" .
386	   386	
387	   387	aqComponent:app-001
388	   388	  aqCommon:createdBy      aqUser:u-ada ;
389	   389	  aqCommon:lastModifiedBy aqUser:u-grace .
390	   390	```
391	   391	
392	   392	Both edges are cleared by `del_component_metadata` and `del_reference_metadata`,
393	   393	alongside `rdf:type`, `common/parent` and `common/workspace`, because
394	   394	`del_all_about` removes only literal-object triples: a row that changed hands would
395	   395	otherwise name both authors.
396	   396	
397	   397	Being object-valued has one model-level consequence. `common/createdBy` and
398	   398	`common/lastModifiedBy` are no longer `aq:BuiltInFieldType` and no longer sit under
399	   399	`aq:Field`. `aq:Field` is an `owl:DatatypeProperty`, and OWL 2 DL requires object
400	   400	and data properties to be disjoint, so an object-valued built-in cannot be a
401	   401	sub-property of it — the same reason `common/parent` and `common/workspace` are not.
402	   402	Their SHACL shapes are `sh:class common/User` rather than `sh:datatype xsd:string`.
403	   403	
404	   404	`global_field.type = 'User'` values are still `xsd:string`. They are user ids too
405	   405	and should become edges to these same resources; that is not mapped yet.
406	   406	
407	   407	### Emitting a user exactly once
408	   408	
409	   409	The resources are emitted **once per target**, never per row. Both bulk paths send
410	   410	`X-GraphLake-Skip-Duplicate-Check`, which turns off GraphLake's duplicate check, so
411	   411	a type triple asserted once per component would be *stored* once per component: on
412	   412	this repo's dev org that is 33,716 copies of one triple for a single user. Each
413	   413	path uses its own mechanism:
414	   414	
415	   415	```text
416	   416	full sync         one directory read, before components, per target (main and each
417	   417	                  branch, since each commits by MOVEing its own graph over the
418	   418	                  target's live graph). The author half of its scope is a `select
419	   419	                  distinct` over the audit columns of the live tables
420	   420	history backfill  the same, with the author pass reading the history mirrors as
421	   421	                  well. Recorded once before the first month as one `user:<id>`
422	   422	                  entity in the carried state, and written nowhere else: a month's
423	   423	                  snapshot is materialised from that state, and the backfill does
424	   424	                  not touch the head
425	   425	CDC streaming     per row, resolving each author against the settings database
426	   426	                  through a cache that holds misses as well as hits. This is the
427	   427	                  only path that can add a user between full syncs: the CDC stream
428	   428	                  carries the org schema, and the directory is elsewhere. It does
429	   429	                  not skip the duplicate check, so the store collapses the repeats
430	   430	```
431	   431	
432	   432	The two author passes differ deliberately. A full sync writes live state, so a
433	   433	live-only pass is right. Replay materialises entities that have since been deleted —
434	   434	a component removed last year is written into every month before its deletion — and
435	   435	its author may appear in no live row, so a live-only pass there would leave that
436	   436	component's `createdBy` edge pointing at an untyped IRI.
437	   437

   169
